key_insight: ExpRL turns human-written solutions into hidden reward scaffolds, using an LLM judge to give dense process or outcome rewards for on-policy reasoning during mid-training.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical way to prime LLMs for harder reasoning tasks without manually curating training traces, and can improve initialization for later sparse-reward RL.
method: Sample reasoning from the original prompt, not from reference solutions.
Use a judge LLM to compare the trace to the hidden reference and assign process-level or outcome-level rewards.
Reinforce partial progress and useful intermediate reasoning behaviors with dense signals.
evidence_signal: In challenging math reasoning tasks, ExpRL outperforms SFT, sparse-reward GRPO, and self-distillation, and it also improves initialization for later sparse-reward RL; mixed-domain results suggest broader applicability.
watch_item: Because the method depends on judge-generated rubrics and LLM evaluation, performance may be sensitive to judge quality, reward design, and reference coverage.
paper_title: ExpRL: Exploratory RL for LLM Mid-Training
